name: r1_silvianus_ring_curse_v2.mp4
title: He Cursed a Thief on a Sheet of Lead
desc:
Roman Britain: a man called Silvianus loses a gold ring and curses the thief on a lead tablet at the temple of Nodens (Lydney Park). A gold ring found near Silchester names the suspect, Senicianus. Tolkien later wrote a note on the god's name. Did it inspire the One Ring? That is a legend; nobody can prove it.

The real One Ring?

title: 57,470 Casualties in One Day. Tolkien Was There.
desc:

Did you know Tolkien was there?

name: r3_both_rings_were_round.mp4
title: "Both Rings Were Round", Said Tolkien
desc:
Norse legend has its own cursed ring: the dwarf Andvari's ring in the Volsunga saga, which ruins everyone who owns it. Wagner built an opera cycle on it. When a translator compared his Ring to Wagner's, Tolkien replied: "Both rings were round, and there the resemblance ceases." Many scholars are not so sure.

Who is right?

name: r4_gandalf_in_viking_poem.mp4
title: Gandalf Is a Name From a Viking Poem
desc:
The Old Norse Voluspa (Poetic Edda, Codex Regius, Iceland, c. 1270) has a list of dwarf names: Durin, Dvalin, Thorin, Fili, Kili, Gloin, even Oakenshield... and Gandalf (Gandalfr). Almost all of the Hobbit dwarves, and Gandalf, come from it. Tolkien said so himself.

Which name surprised you?
